This is not an implemented raw finder or a whole-network extension. No existing fixed-pool global theorem is broadened by this receipt.

## Label identity and terminal reward

If an ordinary type-i particle restores the protected D token, move its ordinary identity to the old token. Exactly one ordinary identity changes type, from i to the old token's actual terminal type. Physical counts are unchanged. If the old token itself restores D, no ordinary identity moves. This requires that ordinary particles did not evolve during the deleted excursion; otherwise the one-exchange accounting is insufficient.

Use the actual FIRST terminal event, including other terminal exits, as the killing time. The terminal ordinary-restoration counter, including its mark at that time, has expectation equal to its stopped intensity integral. With frozen y_i this is y_i E integral h_i. A nonnegative supersolution -Q_y psi_i>=h_i bounds the integral by psi_i: localized Dynkin gives the inequality up to bounded stopping, and nonnegativity/Fatou removes localization. The entrance sum therefore bounds the entire trace exchange intensity by b_i y_i. This is a terminal probability statement, not independence of competing exit times. At y_i=0 the exchange is absent and no division by y_i is needed.

Thus time-only ingress cannot replace this certificate.

Deleting completed excursions creates their actual exit kernel in the trace, provided the state includes all persistent phase metadata and terminal outputs are retained. Ordinary labels retain their types throughout the excursion, except possibly at its terminal restoration. If an ordinary label of type i restores D, protect that restored particle and give its ordinary label identity to the old token, whose terminal type is p. The ordinary population has undergone exactly i -> p. If the old token restores D itself, the ordinary population is unchanged. This is an identity convention, not alteration of a physical reaction. It preserves every physical count. It requires exactly one token and the stated frozen-ordinary-phase structure; general ordinary rearrangements cannot be silently included.

Thus the obstacle is not intrinsically a multi-label simultaneous reset. It is the intensity of this single-label exchange in the traced clock.

# Finite phase-scaled reward acquisition without a population-dependent inverse

30 October 2026. Local sufficient compiler rule building on REWARD_WEIGHTED_TOKEN_EXCHANGE.md; no whole-network extension.

Let Q0 be a fixed finite rational transient generator for token phases, including its own-restoration/terminal exits. Let s(y)>0 be a frozen configuration scale. Suppose the actual killed excursion generator is

    Q_y=s(y) Q0-diag(k(y)),   k>=0,

where k includes every ordinary-restoration exit and any additional terminal marks. Ordinary type-i per-particle restoring intensities obey 0<=h_i(p,y)<=hbar_i(p). Entrance intensities into each phase obey sum_{e:p_e=p} lambda_e(y)<=s(y) ell_p, with fixed ell>=0. All frozen-ordinary and actual-stopping conventions of the main note remain necessary.

Solve the constant rational system

    -Q0 t_i=hbar_i.

Transience implies t_i>=0. Put psi_i(p,y)=t_i(p)/s(y). Then pointwise

    -Q_y psi_i=hbar_i+diag(k)t_i/s >=h_i,
    sum_e lambda_e psi_i(p_e)<=ell dot t_i=:b_i.

Hence every summed exchange out of ordinary type i has full trace intensity <=b_i y_i. No small-return probability, bounded entry rate, or population-dependent matrix inversion is needed. The diagonal killing term is useful, not a perturbation to be assumed small. Rational acquisition consists of a finite graph reachability check for Q0, exact linear solves, and raw rate factorization/inequality certificates for s, ell, hbar. Factoring a common scale is sufficient, not necessary.

Illustrative exact algebra (abstract phase kernel, not a new reaction-network claim):

    Q0 = [[-3, 2], [1, -4]],  hbar=(1,2),  ell=(2,1).
    t=(4/5,7/10),  b=23/10.

Thus for every s>0 and every nonnegative diagonal killing vector, entrance rates bounded by (2s,s) give total ordinary-i exchange rate <=(23/10)y_i. If an ordinary restoring intensity grows as s instead of remaining <=hbar, this rule does not apply. The failed time-only example in the main note is precisely of that type.

This is ordinary killed-chain reward/resolvent algebra, used as a constructive certificate rather than a novelty claim. Before global use the actual physical model still has to supply the required trace-clock scaling, retain non-restoration terminal outputs, and satisfy all other graded signed-cycle interfaces.
